Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Department of Defense (DoD), Office of the Chief Prosecutor (OCP) of Military Commissions. The OCP is responsible for recommending and prosecuting cases for trial before Military Commissions in accordance with the Military Commissions Act of 2009. The OCP is a component of the Office of Military Commissions and is comprised of the Chief Prosecutor, Prosecutors, and other persons under the supervision of the Chief Prosecutor.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Washington Headquarters Services (WHS) is a world-class service organization, with a dynamic workforce and unwavering commitment to service excellence. WHS is the essential services provider for the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), Department of Defense (DoD) agencies, and offices in the National Capital Region.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as a senior prosecutor, with responsibility for investigating, researching, and preparing all aspects of and prosecuting highly complex international terrorism cases before Military Commissions These commissions are a unique military trial forum authorized by the Military Commissions Act of 2009. The incumbent provides legal research and analysis in evolving areas of law that require adapting military, domestic, foreign, and international legal principles to specific uses and problems, and creative thinking to develop well-articulated positions on the many legal issues that arise during the course of Military Commissions litigation. Investigates and prepares cases for trial. The incumbent interacts directly and routinely with senior interagency investigative and intelligence counterparts. This includes coordinating with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the National Security Agency (NSA), the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA), the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), and other investigative entities. Serves as a senior staff adviser to the Chief Prosecutor, as needed, based on extensive trial-related experienced. Sets overall legal strategies for various trials. This includes conducting all aspects of investigations, legal research, pre-trial preparation, litigation of motions, witness interviews/preparation, and presentation of facts before Military Commissions. If selected, Federal employees currently serving in the competitive service must acknowledge that they will voluntarily leave the competitive service by accepting an offer of employment for an excepted service positions.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. The Department of the Navy (DON) Office of the General Counsel (OGC) has been serving the Department since 1941 and is committed to developing innovative legal solutions to the business and other challenges facing the Navy and Marine Corps to enhance the war fighting capability of the Naval Service. You will find our attorneys stationed across the United States and worldwide, working with Navy and Marine Corps personnel wherever the Department's business is conducted. DON OGC also offers a great place to build a career. Based on the DON OGC annual employee survey, DON OGC attorneys consistently reports the highest marks for workforce collegiality, cooperation, and meaningful, high quality work. This serves as the Counsel, Naval Audit Service (NAVAUDSVC). This is a GS-15 position within the DON OGC as part of the Deputy General Counsel's office.
MajorDuties: You will provide legal advice on difficult and extremely complex problems; advise clients on matters, and cases brought by or against the DON.
You will interpret laws, rulings and regulations for the DON; and analyze the probable outcomes of cases and matters using knowledge of legal precedents.
You will present and summarize cases; draft and interpret laws and legislation; and evaluate findings and develop strategies and arguments in preparation of matters and cases.
You will prepare legal briefs and opinions for matters and cases or negotiate settlements in the appropriate forum.
You will will represent and advocate for the DON and provide legal advice and counsel, in the form of oral advice and written opinions, in one or more of the subject areas of law.

Details.OtherInformation: NAVAUDSVC is headed by the Auditor General of the Navy (AUDGEN) and is responsible for internal auditing within the DON, and audits both appropriated and non-appropriated organizations, programs, activities, and functions within DON. The Counsel, NAVAUDSVC answers any legal questions and provides guidance on legal issues arising from such audits as well as from the activities of the NAVAUDSVC. The principal clients are the AUDGEN, the Deputy AUDGEN, and the Assistant AUDGEN(s), as well as employees throughout the NAVAUDSVC. As appropriate, the Counsel will be expected to work with the attorneys assigned to the Acquisition Integrity Office and other legal offices with the DON Office of the General Counsel (OGC) organization. Most legal advice must be in written form and the attorney must be able to support such advice, orally and in writing, through various levels of the DON as audit issues are resolved. The incumbent will also serve as the NAVAUDSVC Ethics Officer. Information about the Naval Audit Service may be found at: https://www.secnav.navy.mil/navaudsvc. The anticipated position is the Counsel, who serves as the NAVAUDSVC'S primary legal expert. The incumbent of this position provides the full range of legal support primarily in the fields of federal contracting, fiscal, federal civilian personnel, government ethics and standards of conduct, and Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)/Privacy Act law. The incumbent also may advise on matters involving real and personal property, environmental, criminal, labor, and business and commercial law.. Audits frequently uncover issues either: (i) in the financial management area, involving all aspects of fund availability, obligation, expenditure, transfer, and reimbursement, or (ii) related to contracting activities. As all DON activities can be audited, in addition to general knowledge of fiscal and procurement policies and procedures, the attorney filling this position may be required to advise on unique fiscal constraints and procurement methods used by individual DON activities to perform unique services or acquire unique commodities or services. Collaboration and Integration. Senior officers have a responsibility to share information and knowledge to achieve results, and in that regard, are expected to build effective networks and alliances with key peers and stakeholders across the IC and/or with other U.S. Government (USG), state, local, tribal and foreign officials, as appropriate; actively engage these peers and stakeholders; involve them in key decisions; and effectively leverage these networks and alliances to achieve significant results. Senior officers are expected to create an environment that promotes employee engagement, collaboration, integration, information and knowledge sharing, and the candid, open exchange of diverse points of view.
